top_gainers.name: Semtech
top_gainers.narrative: Semtech jumped 11% (part of a ~39% three-week run) after record Q2 FY27 revenue of $341.9M (+33% y/y, +17% q/q) with margin expansion, driven by optical-networking and AI-data-center demand plus a planned divestiture of its lower-margin cellular module business (expected to lift gross margins ~500bp). Roth Capital, UBS, Northland and Baird all raised price targets ($182-$300 range) on the print.

top_gainers.name: DigitalOcean
top_gainers.narrative: DigitalOcean's decline is a valuation reset despite strong fundamentals (a 73% earnings surprise still triggered an 11% post-earnings drop) - the concerning part is $570.5M of insider selling over the past 12 months with zero insider buying, on a still cash-flow-negative business. Worth watching, not a clean bounce case.

top_gainers.name: IES Holdings

Debt-free with $310.6M in marketable securities.

top_losers.name: J.B. Hunt
top_losers.narrative: J.B. Hunt fell 13.3% - one of its worst trading days since its 1983 IPO - after warning Q3 earnings would drop 5-10% from Q2 on two cost pressures: diesel hit a record national average of $6.31/gallon, and the company flagged $25M in additional driver expenses (recruiting, training, signing bonuses). Fuel surcharges eventually pass through to customers, but with a lag, leaving J.B. Hunt to absorb the cost now. This is the freight-and-logistics-sector mirror image of this pull's oil/energy story: the same crude/refined-product price spike hurting consumers at the pump is a direct margin hit for a fuel-intensive trucker.

bounce.name: Enova International, Inc.
bounce.thesis: Enova crashed ~22-25% on Sept 15 after withdrawing its OCC/Fed regulatory applications for the $369M Grasshopper Bancorp acquisition, with the CEO citing a lack of clear standards for nonbanks seeking to become banks. This is a real, abandoned strategic deal, not noise - but the company reiterated Q3 and full-year 2026 guidance unchanged (revenue +25% y/y, adjusted EPS +30% y/y) the same day, meaning the core lending business's outlook wasn't cut. Bounce thesis rests on the deal's collapse being a strategic setback rather than a signal of operational trouble.

citations.title: Enova International (ENVA) Stock Plummets 25% After Abandoning $369M Grasshopper Bank Acquisition

value.name: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions
value.thesis: Kratos is down 37% YTD despite a strong defense backlog and hypersonics revenue guided to ~$400M in 2026 and $700M+ in 2027 (MACH-TB program funding), plus recent $20M and $35M contract wins. Value case: the stock's multiple has compressed even as the forward revenue/earnings trajectory improved.

value.name: Fiserv
value.thesis: Fiserv is down 64% over the past year after slashing 2026 guidance to roughly flat organic revenue, driven partly by Argentina inflation normalization. Real fundamental deterioration, not pure sentiment - but at 72% below one fair-value estimate ($48.65 vs $174.38 GuruFocus GF Value), this is a case where the market may have overcorrected for a genuine but bounded problem.

citations.title: Fiserv stock tumbles after cutting 2026 guidance

value.name: Boston Scientific
value.thesis: Boston Scientific is down ~60% from its September 2025 all-time high after a cyberattack disruption and slowing electrophysiology/WATCHMAN growth forced a guidance cut to 6.5-8% organic growth. Real operational hit, but the growth-rate cut (not a growth reversal) at a much lower valuation ahead of an Oct 28 earnings report is the value setup here.

citations.title: Has BSX Stock Fallen Far Enough To Buy?
